items.title: DSA kya hai aur interview mein kaise use hota hai
items.one_idea: DSA is two things, a data structure (how data is organised) and an algorithm (the steps that use it), and an interview checks whether your steps still work when the data is huge: 10 lakh sorted names take up to 1,000,000 checks one by one but about 20 with halving.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: 10 लाख names में एक name, 20 steps में कैसे ढूँढोगे?
items.hook_source: carried-over LearnAI hypothesis, first DSA test; hookscore 46.5 WEAK, no DEALBREAKER
items.visual_idea: A long row of name tiles with a magnifier moving one tile at a time and a step counter climbing toward 1,000,000, crossed out in red; then the same row halved again and again, the counter stopping at 20; chips DATA STRUCTURE (the row) and ALGORITHM (the halving moves) land on the objects when named.
items.everyday_anchor: Finding one contact among 10 lakh saved numbers: sorted list opened in the middle like a dictionary.
items.example: EXAMPLE (researcher ran it): 10 lakh sorted ints, target last: one-by-one 1000000 comparisons (worst case), halving 20. Printed: 1000000 20 True. Counts, not seconds.
facts_to_verify: Run both searches on 1,000,000 sorted ints and show real printed counts (1000000 and 20).
Amazon claim only: its page says learn how to approach data structures and algorithms in your interview; no claim about all companies, no claim about why.
The why-interviews-ask line is labelled as our own reasoning.
Halving needs a SORTED list; said on screen.
